title: Process pairs
text: A primary and backup run on different CPUs. If the primary fails, the backup can take over. A surviving backup does not mean all CPU capacity is restored.

title: Takeover
text: A backup assumes the primary role after failure. Correlate takeover messages with the originating CPU event before opening separate investigations.

title: CPU loss on NonStop
header: concept · CPU loss on NonStop · cpu
text: Redundant processes can continue after a CPU halt while unpaired server processes on that CPU are lost. Check survivor utilization and customer-facing latency.

title: Pathway server classes
text: A named group of equivalent server processes serves a workload. Inspect running count, maximum, queue and response time together.

title: Pathway links
text: Links connect requesters to server processes. A link-grant failure can indicate unavailable capacity rather than a broken link manager.

title: NUMSTATIC versus MAXSERVERS
text: NUMSTATIC keeps a configured floor of static servers. MAXSERVERS limits total instances. A lower static floor can coexist with more running dynamic servers; the floor cannot exceed the ceiling.

title: TMF audit trails
text: TMF records transaction changes for recovery. Trail pressure can constrain new work even when CPU utilization is otherwise healthy.

title: Audit overflow thresholds
text: TORBANK uses synthetic guards at 80% overflow and 90% begin-transaction disable. These are demo configuration values; read the live trail before proposing action.

title: N-1 headroom
text: Ask whether the node can carry its workload after losing one CPU. Baton projects each loss using backup placement and lost server capacity. A risk warning can precede any current service breach.

title: Reading CPU busy
text: Utilization shows how occupied a processor is during the measurement interval. Compare survivors, batch placement and service latency; high busy alone does not identify the cause.

title: EMS collectors
text: Collectors gather subsystem events into an event log for distribution. Keep event provenance when reducing repeated messages into episodes.

title: EMS distributors
text: Printing distributors produce operator-readable event text. Consumer distributors expose events to applications, and forwarding distributors send events to another node.

title: p95 service latency
text: 95% of sampled requests complete at or below this value. Compare with the expected calendar band and timeout rate rather than reading the average alone.

title: Calendar baseline bands
text: A service band represents expected behavior at this simulated time and load. Black Friday demand differs from an ordinary weekday. A synthetic band is not a production guarantee.

title: Queues and capacity
text: A queue forms when offered work exceeds available service capacity. Inspect running versus maximum, CPU load and recent changes to distinguish lost capacity from a configured ceiling.

title: Protected processes
text: TORBANK protects PATHMON, disk processes and link managers. A generic suspend request cannot bypass target protection. Use the approved escalation path.

title: Two-person approval
text: An impactful T2 change needs distinct approvals and at least one senior operator or expert. The first approval remains visible while the action waits.

title: Earned autonomy
text: The trust ledger records outcomes per catalog template, parameter class and role. L2 permits approved read-only automation after an expert grants it; an eligible counter does not grant itself.

title: Verifying recovery
text: The CPU-loss scenario requires ATM p95 back within its band for 60 simulated seconds and the hottest CPU below 90%. A single improved sample is not recovery.

title: Temporary mitigations and undo
header: concept · Temporary mitigations and undo · governance
text: Suspending batch and adding static servers buy time. Record inverses, verify service recovery, and retain a follow-up to restore configuration after hardware repair.
